Introduction This implementation guide provides guidance that is derived from the following WHO guidelines: Medical Eligibility Criteria for Contraceptive Use. 5th ed World Health Organization (WHO). Selected Practice Recommendations for Contraceptive Use Family Planning: A Global Handbook for Providers (2018 update) Contraceptive eligibility for women at high risk of HIV Adolescent job aid: a handy desk reference tool for primary level health workers WHO recommendations on adolescent sexual and reproductive health and rights For a complete listing of the artifacts defined in this implementation guide, refer to the Artifact Index. This guide was converted from its original XML/JSON sources to FSH on 2026-11-10, and some profiles and value sets were corrected along the way. The Conversion to FSH page lists every change, with the changes in meaning first. Implementation content, as well as a complete offline copy of this implementation guide can be found on the Downloads page. Note that the content of this implementation guide is draft material that has not yet been tested or validated for use in production environments.

On 2026-11-10 this IG was converted from an XML ImplementationGuide ( input/fp-cds.xml plus JSON resources) to FSH, built with sushi (0 errors). This page lists every change, with the pull request that made it. Changes in meaning (read these first) These change what the profiles and value sets allow. They were approved by the repository owner as draft fixes. Items marked guess need review by the content owners. In the Requested profile the ICD-10 Z30.9 code moved from device.type to device . 6 contraception-issues-and-concerns-values ICD-10 N89.8 listed twice ("Spotting or light bleeding", "Unexplained vaginal bleeding") listed once, displays joined with " / " ( guess ) 6 medicaleligibilityconditions-values CIEL 159276 (DVT, PE), CIEL 144475 (Stroke, Stroke (history of CVA)), ICD-11 BD72 (DVT, History of DVT, History of PE), 8B20 (Stroke, Stroke (history of CVA)), 5A14 (Diabetes, Nephropathy, Retinopathy) each listed more than once each listed once, displays joined with " / " ( guess : some of these probably need different codes, for example DVT and PE) 6 12 elements in 11 profiles (table below) cardinality looser than the base resource allows the base cardinality 5 deliveryMethod extension Extension.extension 0..1 next to a value Extension.extension 0..0 (a simple extension cannot also have sub-extensions) 5 Cardinalities brought back to the base ( 5): Profile Element Before After (base) --- --- --- --- CarePlan (Backup Contraceptive Method) activity.detail.code 0.. 0..1 CarePlan (Exit Contraceptive Method) activity.detail.code 0.. 0..1 DeviceUseStatement (Exit) device.type 0.. 0..1 (later replaced by the Device profile, see above) MedicationStatement (Current Medication) medication[x] 0.. 1..1 MedicationStatement (Exit Contraceptive Method) medication[x] 0.. 1..1 MedicationStatement (Requested Contraceptive Method) medication[x] 0..1 1..1 Observation (Breastfeeding Status) value[x] 0.. 0..1 Observation (Medical Eligibility) code 0..1 1..1 Observation (Reason for Stopping Contraception) valueCodeableConcept 0.. 0..1 Procedure (Exit Contraceptive Method) code 0.. 0..1 Procedure (Service Provided) status 0..1 1..1 Changes with no change in meaning The conversion itself ( 3) kept every resource as it was. The JSON that sushi generated was compared with the original JSON: All 15 value sets and the deliveryMethod extension: identical, field by field. (At that stage the extension and two value sets were still kept as JSON; 5 and 6 later moved them to FSH with the changes above.) The code system: identical apart from count: 9 , which sushi adds. Profiles: snapshots were built for both versions with fhir-snapshot-generator against hl7.fhir.r4.core 4.0.1, and 25 of 26 are identical. The one difference: CarePlan.activity.detail.extension gets the default slicing by url , which the IG Publisher normally adds to extension elements anyway. The tool could not snapshot 3 profiles; their differentials differ only by cardinalities equal to the base. The ImplementationGuide keeps the XML IG's id, canonical, version, name, title, publisher, contact, jurisdiction, page tree and parameters. The menu is now generated from sushi-config.yaml with the same entries. How the raw JSON differs in form, without changing meaning: Difference Why --- --- min / max equal to the base are left out (60 places in 29 profiles) sushi only writes what changes the base. Observation.valueX is written as value[x] with only X FSH has no renamed-path form; the snapshot is the same. Reason for Stopping Contraception: value[x] limited to CodeableConcept or string, with two type slices same constraints in sushi's form. CodeSystem.count added sushi fills it in.
